HipKittens (HazyResearch/HipKittens at 8cde3dd, kernels/cdna4): bugs found while bringing its
kernels up in Volta. Line numbers are in the upstream sources. Status says how each finding was
established: "Volta" means a Volta run decided it; otherwise it comes from reading the source and
the compiled assembly, and the Volta case that should decide it is named.

1. Lazy rescale scales O after only one of the four P.V chunks (Volta)
   Where: attn/gqa/kernel.cpp and kernel_d64.cpp lines 266-284 and 338-356;
          attn/gqa_causal/kernel.cpp and kernel_d64.cpp lines 355-373 and 433-451.
   The four mma_AtB(o_reg, subtile_inplace<16>(v_reg, k), ...) calls split P_{t-1} V_{t-1} over
   keys 0-15, 16-31, 32-47 and 48-63. The first runs before the lazy-rescale branch and the other
   three after it, so when the branch rescales, the code computes
       O = s (O_old + P[0:16] V[0:16]) + P[16:64] V[16:64],   s = exp2(m_prev - m_new),
   where every term was computed against the old max and all of them need the factor s. The
   normaliser is scaled consistently, so numerator and denominator disagree. In the compiled
   gqa kernel, four MFMAs precede the s_cbranch on the vote and the scaling block jumps back to
   the remaining twelve.
   Effect: wrong O for every query row whose running max grows by more than RESCALE_THRESHOLD
   (8, in log2-scaled score units) at a lazily checked KV tile; 48 keys of that tile are
   weighted 1/s too much (1/s >= 256 for the triggering row). Random-normal test inputs never
   take this path, which is why the upstream tests pass.
   Fix: issue the other three mma_AtB calls before the if/else, with the first.
   Volta, on workgroup 0 (256 query rows, 512 keys, its first query row compared): with both
   loop branches forced to rescale, attn_gqa_rescale and attn_gqa_d64_rescale REJECT (numeric
   counterexample at O[0]); with the fix, attn_gqa_rescale_fixed and attn_gqa_d64_rescale_fixed
   ACCEPT; forced to keep the max, attn_gqa_skip and attn_gqa_d64_skip ACCEPT. All are race free.

2. Stale scale_vec applied unconditionally to the normaliser in the epilogue (Volta)
   Where: attn/gqa/kernel.cpp:386 and attn/gqa_causal/kernel.cpp:481, and the same lines of
   both kernel_d64.cpp files: mul(norm_vec, norm_vec, scale_vec) with no pending_scale guard.
   The fast path never resets scale_vec, so if the last rescale happened before the loop's
   final iteration, the normaliser is multiplied by that old factor a second time (the in-loop
   update is guarded; the compiled loop selects 1.0 with v_cndmask, the epilogue does not).
   Effect: the denominator is too small by s for the affected rows.
   Fix: guard the multiply with pending_scale, or ones(scale_vec) in the fast path.
   Volta, as for 1 and with 1's fix: the loop's first branch forced to rescale and its second to
   keep the max, attn_gqa_mixed and attn_gqa_d64_mixed REJECT (numeric counterexample at O[0];
   about 20 and 6 minutes, the solver's attempt before the oracle) and attn_gqa_mixed_fixed and
   attn_gqa_d64_mixed_fixed, the epilogue's multiply guarded with pending_scale, ACCEPT.

3. Unchecked size preconditions in the forward attention kernels (medium; non-default sizes)
   The epilogue assumes the loop ended at j = N/64 - 3, i.e. N/64 even and at least 4: for odd
   N/64 (N = 320) it recomputes QK with the last K tile twice, pairs P(K_{n-1}) with V_{n-2} and
   counts the last tile twice in the normaliser; N = 128 loads K tile 2 out of range. The grid
   needs N to be a multiple of 256, else the last workgroup reads Q and writes O/L past N. No
   static_assert guards either. Same structure in attn/gqa_backwards/attn_fwd_non_causal.cpp and
   attn/gqa_causal_backwards/attn_fwd_causal.cpp.

4. attn/repro/attn_kernel.cpp is a skeleton that races and does not compile
   It is the load stage of a chunked linear-attention kernel with its body a TODO. No s_barrier
   anywhere while every wave reads LDS tiles other waves loaded (read-after-write races), `tic`
   is never toggled (write-after-read races on the next iteration), waves 2-7 issue no V load so
   their vmcnt waits wait for the wrong loads, and `uint32_t swizzled_offsets_V[0]` is a
   zero-length array that is written and read (clang rejects it: "zero-length arrays are not
   permitted in HIP device code").

5. Build breaks
   gemm/bf16fp32/micros/producer_consumer/{16x32,32x16}/micro_02_2stage_8c4p.cpp,
   micro_03_3stage_8c4p.cpp and micro_04_2stage_12c4p.cpp call kittens::warpgroupid, which the
   library no longer defines.

6. Configuration trap: attn/gqa_causal/kernel_d64.cpp defaults ATTN_D to 128 (low)
   Its `#ifndef ATTN_D` fallback is 128, unlike gqa/kernel_d64.cpp's 64. Built through its
   Makefile (which passes -DATTN_D) it is correct; built without it, the "d64" file silently
   becomes a head-dim-128 kernel (attend_ker<128>) that, given head-dim-64 tensors, reads the
   neighbouring heads' columns and writes O into them.

7. 256x256 GEMM (16x32 tiles) reads Bs[1][0] one barrier too early: a data race (Volta)
   Where: gemm/bf16fp32/256_256_64_32_with16x32.cpp, main loop, the fourth MMA phase:
   `load(B_tile_0, subtile_inplace(Bs[1][0], ...))` before `s_waitcnt vmcnt(6); s_barrier`.
   Waves 4-7 pass one s_barrier more at the start (`if (warp_row == 1)`), so they trail waves 0-3
   by one barrier: a tile every wave loads and waits for at a phase's first barrier may be read
   from the next phase on, as every other tile is. Bs[1][0] is read in the very phase that waits
   for it, before the wait: a wave's ds_read races with its own pending buffer_load ... lds, and
   waves 0-3 read waves 4-7's quarter before those waves' wait. The compiled loop has no other
   vmcnt wait in between. It happens in every iteration (and after the prologue's load).
   Effect: B_tile_0 may hold stale LDS data, the previous K tile's, for the next C_accum[0][0]
   MMA; on hardware only when that load takes longer than three MMA phases.
   Fix: read Bs[1][0] at the start of the fifth phase, before As[1][0].
   Volta: gemm_256_16x32 REJECT (memory conflict, LDS byte 98304: wave 0's slice of Bs[1][0],
   its prologue load and the loop's ds_read); gemm_256_16x32_fixed ACCEPT. Moving the read only
   after the phase's own wait still races (byte 102400, wave 4's slice), as the stagger implies.

8. 192x256 GEMM kernelv2 waits for too few loads on waves 4-7: a data race (Volta)
   Where: gemm/bf16fp32/micros/192x256/kernelv2.cpp, every `s_waitcnt vmcnt(N)` (4, 6, 2).
   kernel.cpp waits with vmcnt(0); kernelv2 tightens the waits to the 256x256 kernel's counts,
   which assume two buffer_load ... lds per tile per wave. A 96x64 bf16 A tile is 12288 bytes:
   one 8192-byte load across all 512 threads plus a 4096-byte leftover that only waves 0-3
   issue, so waves 4-7 issue one load per A tile and their vmcnt(N) leaves older loads pending.
   In the prologue, wave 4's vmcnt(4) completes only Bs[0][0], not its slice of As[0][0], which
   waves 0-3 read after the next barrier.
   Effect: stale A data in the first MMAs (and likewise later in the loop).
   Fix: kernel.cpp's vmcnt(0), or counts per wave from the loads it issues.
   Volta: gemm_192v2 REJECT (memory conflict, LDS byte 4096: wave 4's slice of As[0][0]);
   gemm_192 (kernel.cpp) ACCEPT.

Checked and not bugs
- softmax (Volta): the compiled expf rescales by f32(e^-64) past its underflow bound, so it is
  not exactly the softmax over the reals; it is within 1/1000 of it: at 32 x 32 (softmax_d32),
  `volta extract lean --tolerance 1/1000` gives 1024 statements, all proved, accepted by Volta's
  Lean check and replayed by leanchecker (target/lean/hipkittens_softmax32).
- rotary (Volta ACCEPT): waits on lgkmcnt after global loads, but the compiler's own vmcnt
  waits order the loads; all 4096 outputs proved equal to rotary.spec.
- Forward attention (gqa, head dims 64 and 128; Volta on workgroup 0 for each forced branch path
  above): race free (LDS double buffering, waits and barriers) and equal to attention_d64.spec /
  attention_d128.spec on its first query row once bugs 1 and 2 are fixed. Read correct but not run:
  the causal mask, L_vec (natural-log LSE), the GQA head mapping, and the always-rescale forward
  kernels of the backward directories (their mul_col follows the whole MMA).
- GEMMs (Volta ACCEPT on workgroup 0, every output of its tile): 256x256 with32x16 and 192x256
  kernel.cpp at M = 512 / 384, N = K = 256 (the main loop's K tiles and the epilogue's).

How the global loads are checked
- The attention kernels' K and V loads and the 16x32 GEMM's A and B loads go through buffer
  descriptors from make_srsrc(ptr, range, row_stride), which sets the stride, CACHE_SWIZZLE and
  SWIZZLE_EN (the other GEMMs call it without a row stride: plain raw buffers). The
  CDNA4 ISA (9.1.5.2) defines a swizzled access's address through an element size that its buffer
  descriptor (table 48) has no field for, and range-checks only unswizzled raw buffers (9.1.5.1),
  so it does not define what these accesses read. The kernels compute linear byte offsets and
  pass HipKittens' tests on MI355X, so cases.py drops the row stride from those calls
  (`unswizzled`): Volta checks them as linear raw buffers.

Open (not yet run in Volta)
- The causal attention kernels (gqa_causal) and the backward kernels (buffer loads into AGPRs).
- producer_consumer micro_05/09_async spin on LDS counters (ds_add_u32), which Volta does not
  model. The FP8/MXFP8 GEMMs need the f8f6f4 MFMAs.
